nodes.name: Normalize order
nodes.notes: Why Code: validates the Shopify payload and applies field fallbacks no Set node can express

parameters.query:
-- Records a newly seen order once. A replayed delivery (Shopify's own retry, or an owner
-- retry from the n8n UI) is suppressed by ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING instead of raising a
-- duplicate-key error. On the SQL side that's zero rows, but this is an INSERT, not a SELECT, so
-- n8n's Postgres node reports it as one {success: true} item with no order_id, not as zero items.
INSERT INTO orders (order_id, order_number)
VALUES ($1, $2)
ON CONFLICT (order_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING order_id;

nodes.name: Check config
nodes.notes: Why Code: validates the hand-edited config before any order is processed

parameters.content:
## Normalize and deduplicate
Accepts the whole order payload from Shopify orders, normalizes it, and records it once. A replayed delivery for an order already recorded stops right here; only a genuinely new order reaches the rest of the chain.

## Hand off
Loads and validates the current config, then calls Process order once per order without waiting on it, so a slow or failing core run never holds this execution open.

NOTE: an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING order_id that inserts nothing still reports one {success: true} item, because this is not a SELECT — that's why this gate tests order_id, not the item count. If the INSERT actually committed but its response was lost before n8n saw it, a retry returns the same {success: true}, and the order stops here with no alert. Recovery: delete that orders row and re-send it if it was a test order, or add the sheet row by hand if it was a real one.

NOTE: one webhook call carries exactly one order, so .first() on Normalize order's output is always the order this run is processing. Ceiling: a future caller that hands this workflow more than one item at once would still only process the first of them. Upgrade path: read the order from the current item (.item) instead of always taking the first one.
